title: How Israel’s Defenders Use Palestinian Voters As Window Dressing
author: Peter Beinart
content:
_**Editor 's note: **I'm delighted to share this article from Peter Beinart,
one of America's leading Jewish political commentators and author of [The
Beinart Notebook](https://peterbeinart.substack.com/), on Tuesday's Israeli
elections. - **Mehdi**_

On Tuesday, as Israelis cast their ballots, former Biden administration
antisemitism envoy Deborah Lipstadt spied an opportunity for hasbara. At 2:39
pm ET, she
[retweeted](https://x.com/deborahlipstadt/status/2115151352393535572) a video
of Bedouins heading to the polls on camels, and added the caption: "Bedouins
voting? Apartheid? And maybe the kingmakers?" Twelve minutes later, she
[reposted](https://x.com/deborahlipstadt/status/2115154492216005115) an image
of veiled Muslim women supposedly crowded into a polling station alongside the
words: "And again, I ask: apartheid?" (Palestinian politicians
[alleged](https://u.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/arab-alliance-accuses-netanyahu-
of-using-fake-image-to-exaggerate-voter-
turnout/4102627?utm_source=chatgpt.com) that the photo was an AI fake.)

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

For Lipstadt, the images of Palestinian citizens voting proved that Israel's
political system is not racist. But only two hours earlier, Benjamin Netanyahu
had posted an [ad](https://x.com/netanyahu/status/2115124596303352150) using
those same images. And the ad was, well, racist. Alongside the video of voters
on camelback, Netanyahu's ad warned: "They will flock in great numbers to the
polls." Superimposed over the photo of veiled woman, it snarled:
"unprecedented voting rate. For the Arab parties."

Lipstadt tweeted nothing about Netanyahu's ad. Perhaps she just missed it. But
judging by her account on Twitter, she also missed the
[reports](https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/elections/2026-10-15/ty-
article/.premium/netanyahu-smotrich-to-send-activists-to-poll-stations-in-
arab-communities/000001a1-3e4e-d1eb-abe1-7e7e83b90000) earlier this month that
Netanyahu and his Finance Minister, Bezalel Smotrich, were dispatching right-
wing "election observers" to Palestinian polling stations to intimidate
voters. And in late September, she said nothing about the Central Election
Committee's [decision](https://www.timesofisrael.com/election-panel-votes-to-
bar-balad-chief-abu-shehadeh-over-alleged-support-for-terror/) - later
partially reversed by Israel's Supreme Court - to ban Palestinian parties from
running in Israel's elections. Lipstadt loves to praise Israel for granting
its Palestinian citizens the right to vote. She's far less interested in
challenging Israel's leaders when they try to take that right away.

She's not alone. Throughout election day, the same individuals and
organizations who routinely justify Israel's control over roughly 5.5 million
stateless and disenfranchised Palestinians in the West Bank, Gaza Strip, and
East Jerusalem lauded Israel for allowing roughly 2 million Palestinian
citizens to vote in Israel proper. New Jersey Congressman Josh Gottheimer
[tweeted](https://x.com/RepJoshG/status/2115165510320955868) that Israel had
reaffirmed its status as "the only democracy in the region," because "Israel's
Arab citizens, men and women, are turning out in historic numbers to vote."
AIPAC [noted](https://x.com/AIPAC/status/2115195525540544660) that "Jewish,
Christian, Muslim, and Druze Israelis cast their ballots to elect the next
Knesset," which "underscores Israel's diversity and steadfast commitment to
the democratic process." U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee
[gushed](https://x.com/GovMikeHuckabee/status/2115033638182269171) that "Arabs
vote same as Israelis. Contentious process, but it's a democracy!"

How did these boosters react to efforts to intimidate Palestinian voters and
ban Palestinian parties? Judging by their Twitter accounts over the last
month, they reacted the same way Lipstadt did: by staying silent.

This tunnel vision isn't accidental. It's the only way to avoid facing the
contradiction between democracy and Jewish supremacy. Lipstadt, Gottheimer,
Huckabee, and AIPAC celebrate Palestinian voting because it burnishes Israel's
democratic credentials. But in a Jewish state, Palestinian voting is
necessarily limited and conditional. Because Jews must rule, Israel cannot
extend the franchise to Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza since that
would threaten Israel's Jewish electoral majority. And because Jews must rule,
the parties elected by Israel's Palestinian citizens can't be equal partners
in an Israeli government. Challenging these restrictions would require
challenging Jewish statehood itself. Which is why they must be resolutely
ignored.

palestinian?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&action=share)

If Israeli leaders in the coming months form a government that includes
Palestinian parties as junior members, Lipstadt, Gottheimer, Huckabee, and
AIPAC will likely seize on their inclusion to once again praise Israeli
democracy. But that's unlikely. Naftali Bennett and Avigdor Lieberman, two key
figures in the anti-Netanyahu coalition, have [already
pledged](https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2026/10/28/record-arab-vote-
brings-painful-dilemma-israels-opposition/) not to join a government with
Palestinian parties, and the leader of that coalition, Gadi Eisenkot, has
outlined conditions that make such a partnership extremely difficult. They
know that Netanyahu - who now
[claims](https://x.com/netanyahu/status/2115479434169868618) that Palestinian
election fraud stole the elections - would viciously demonize any government
that is not composed solely of Jews. Tragically, it's likely that Netanyahu's
opponents will decide that allowing Palestinian parties even a subordinate
role in government violates the sacred principle of Jewish sovereignty. If
that happens, Lipstadt, Gottheimer, Huckabee, and AIPAC will quietly assent.
Because for them, Israeli democracy is a talking point. Jewish supremacy is
what really counts.

Israel's defenders love using Israel's Palestinian citizens as window
dressing. Just so long as they don't walk through the front door.
